card.name: Dhunuchi dance
card.tagline: A devotional Bengali dance performed with smoking incense burners during Durga Puja.
card.profile: Dhunuchi Nritya is a traditional Bengali Hindu dance performed during puja and aarti ceremonies. It is defined by the use of the dhunuchi, a clay incense burner, and is primarily associated with the celebration of Goddess Durga's victory over Mahishasura. The dance is a communal, living tradition that relies on the percussive power of the dhak drum.
card.insight: During the final days of Durga Puja, a dancer balances a burning incense burner in their mouth while moving to the thunderous, heavy rhythm of the dhak drum.

card.profile_long: Dhunuchi Nritya, also known as Dhunuchi Naach, is a traditional Bengali Hindu dance form that serves as a vital component of devotional practice during puja and aarti ceremonies. Rooted in the cultural landscape of Bengal, the dance is most prominently observed during the festival of Durga Puja, specifically occurring between the days of Ashtami and Dashami. The dance is a physical manifestation of victory and empowerment, commemorating the triumph of Goddess Durga over the demon Mahishasura. The central object of the dance is the dhunuchi, a clay incense burner filled with burning coconut husks and incense. The handling of this object defines the dancer's level of expertise. Beginners typically manage one or two dhunuchis, while experienced practitioners demonstrate their skill by balancing three simultaneously—two held in their hands and one gripped in their mouth. This requires a high degree of coordination and focus, as the dancer moves amidst the smoke and heat of the incense. The musical accompaniment for the dance is strictly instrumental, with no vocal component required. The soundscape is dominated by the dhak, a traditional Bengali drum that produces a loud, heavy, and rhythmic beat. This is complemented by the metallic resonance of the kansor and the ghanta, which add layers of percussive intensity. The dancers align their movements with these heavy, percussive rhythms, creating a synchronized atmosphere of celebration that aims to involve the entire community. Costume plays a significant role in the visual presentation of the dance. Women traditionally wear the garad sari, a garment specifically associated with sacred religious ceremonies and puja. Men typically wear a dhoti paired with a kurta-punjabi, with the dhoti appearing in white or various colors, while the kurta-punjabi varies in hue. Both men and women are often seen carrying a gamcha, a traditional thin, coarse cotton towel, as part of their attire during the performance. The dance is fundamentally communal, designed to draw the community together in a shared spirit of celebration. As the dhak drums beat, the dancers move with the incense burners, creating a sensory experience that bridges the gap between the individual performer and the collective religious observance. The practice remains a living tradition, deeply embedded in the religious and social life of Bengali Hindus, particularly during the high-energy days of Durga Puja.

sections.origins_and_history: Dhunuchi Nritya is a Bengali Hindu traditional dance performed during puja and aarti ceremonies. It celebrates the victory of Goddess Durga over Mahishasura.
sections.how_it_is_danced: The dance involves holding one or two dhunuchis, while experts may hold three (two in hands, one in mouth). It is performed to the rhythm of the dhak, kansor, and ghanta.
sections.music_and_instruments: The music is purely instrumental, featuring the dhak, kansor, and ghanta. These instruments produce loud, heavy sounds.
sections.costume_and_setting: Women wear the garad sari. Men wear dhoti and kurta-punjabi. Both may carry a gamcha.
sections.occasions_and_meaning: Performed during the last days of Durga Puja, specifically between Ashtami and Dashami, to celebrate victory and empowerment.

claims.text: Dhunuchi Nritya or Dhunuchi Naach is a Bengali Hindu traditional dance.
This devotional dance is performed during Hindu puja and aarti ceremonies in Bengal.
The dance is usually performed during the last days of Durga Puja, especially between “Ashtami” and “Dashami”.
Beginners hold one or two of these, while those with more expertise may use three at a time (two in each hand and one held in their mouth).
The main instrument is the Dhak, a traditional Bengali instrument.
The traditional dance-related dress for women is the garad sari, which Bengali Hindu women wear during puja or sacred religious ceremonies.
